title: Watch Don Toliver Revive a Beheaded Ye in Surgical ‘OK’ Video
summary: Yeezy is brought back to life by Dr. Toliver in the Bianca Censori-directed clip.
contentText:
Don Toliver has taken his talents from the studio to the surgery table. The Cactus Jack rapper and Ye (formerly Kanye West ) joined forces for the “OK” video on Tuesday (Aug. 18), which is directed by West’s wife, Bianca Censori.

Donning a slate blue suit, Yeezy is left on the operating table with his head detached. Doctors cut open his midsection, as doves fly out. They remove Ye’s organs, a white balloon, apples and a rose (somehow on fire).

Toliver pops out with a demonic look in his eye. He reattaches Ye’s head to his body, bringing the rapper back to life. West gets equipped with a pair of swords while taking his first breaths. It’s possible Censori’s vision is alluding to the rappers being cloned or possessed.

The Houston native puts the swords to work, killing the doctors in the room off-screen, as viewers are only left to depict the violent shadows. It all comes to a frightening close with the pair staring into the surveillance camera while a baby sheep randomly enters the door.

“OK” landed on the deluxe edition of Ye’s Bully album, which arrived in June. West first released Bully in March, which debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 with 152,000 total album-equivalent units earned.

Ye and Toliver have proven to be dynamic collaborators in the past on tracks like “Moon,” “Broken Road” and Vultures 2 ‘s “Field Trip.”

Yeezy has been performing across the globe throughout 2026. He’s got a few U.S. dates on tap with a New Orleans show slated for Aug. 28 and a pair of homecoming performances at Soldier Field in Chicago on Sept. 3 and Sept. 4.

Don Toliver delivered his OCTANE album in January, which earned him his first No. 1 entry on the Billboard 200. He continues to tease NITROUS as a companion project to OCTANE , which remains without a release date.
